sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Imports for the button
sections.what: Brings in the standard button settings, a type for content, and a helper that joins style names together.
sections.why: Likely reason: lets the button accept all normal button options and add its own on top.

sections.name: ButtonProps
sections.title: Options the button accepts
sections.what: Lists the options a button accepts: a style (primary, secondary, or ghost), a size (small, medium, or large), a loading flag, an optional icon, and the content inside. Any normal button option also works.
sections.why: Likely reason: keeps the allowed choices in one place so every button uses the same ones.
sections.watch_out: The content is required, so a button with no text or content will fail the type check.

sections.name: Button
sections.title: Button appearance and loading state
sections.what: The button itself. Its default style is secondary and its default size is medium. While loading it shows a spinner, hides the icon, and cannot be clicked. When disabled or loading it looks faded.
sections.why: Likely reason: disabling the button while work is running stops repeated clicks during a slow action.
sections.watch_out: The spinner has no text for screen readers, so people using them may not know the button is busy.

summary: A shared button that comes in three styles and three sizes and can show a spinner while work is in progress.
purpose: Gives every button in the app the same look and the same loading behavior.
why: Likely reason: one reusable button keeps the look consistent and avoids repeating the same styling in many places.
how: It takes the style, size, loading state, icon, and content as options, combines the matching style names, and shows a spinner in place of the icon while loading. It disables the button while loading or when disabled, and passes any other standard button options through.
inputs: Options from the caller: style, size, loading flag, optional icon, the content inside the button, and any standard button options such as click handlers.
outputs: A clickable HTML button that looks styled and, while loading, shows a spinning indicator and cannot be clicked.
risks: The spinner has no text for screen readers, so a loading button may be silent to people who use them. Because the content is required, every button must have text or other content.
debug: If a button looks wrong, check the style and size options passed by the caller and the shared button classes in index.css. If a button will not click, check whether loading or disabled is set.
